title: Fix installation and simplify Outask documentation across platforms
scope: Fix the reproduced release-installer EACCES failure caused by an unrelated inaccessible PATH entry; add focused regression coverage; verify first install and command/MCP launch from a fresh supported shell without pre-seeding the command directory; clarify published macOS installation, permission failure handling, stable installed locations and Codex MCP registration in primary and packaged instructions. Preserve unrelated commands/data and explicit user-controlled client configuration. Do not claim the reported real-Mac incident is reproduced without its exact command/stderr; do not bypass sandbox or Gatekeeper restrictions, add project-local installation fallbacks, automatic client configuration or new CLI commands. Owner-authorized documentation correction now includes the full audited project documentation, generated target-specific README/help, corresponding focused checks and release-note validation. Continue in the same v1.1 candidate and preserve the owner's existing Mac test artifact. No remote push/publication authorization is inferred. Owner now explicitly approves one public root installer per destination: Linux install.sh, macOS Install.command, Windows Install.cmd. Move implementation helpers under app/scripts, invoke them directly, remove foreign-platform root launchers, and align help/docs/release notes/local helper/native acceptance. Migrate previous managed layouts without restoring obsolete installer files or deleting unrelated user files. Owner explicitly approves correcting first reads of genuinely uninitialised projects: list/count return empty/zero, consistent shared read APIs, without creating fake tasks/store files or masking missing configured/previously populated stores. Keep max page size 50 and existing safety boundaries; add regression coverage and deliver a fresh uniquely named Mac test archive. Owner now authorises correcting MCP parameter descriptions (ordinary cached-read defaults and page bounds) and preparing the v1.1 release PR under exact final remote-action agreement. Owner also explicitly requests removal of the old GitHub Release v1.0; preserve a local metadata/notes/assets backup and its Git tag. This specific deletion overrides the existing-release immutability rule only for that release.
acceptance: The actual release installer succeeds with a non-searchable unrelated PATH directory, and still refuses an accessible unrelated tasks command; a regression test fails against the original installer.

A native macOS archive acceptance starts with a fresh zsh HOME and PATH without the installed bin directory, runs the documented installer, discovers the installed tasks command in a new login shell and starts MCP by command name; Linux/Windows acceptance remains valid.

Project documentation follows the owner's approved concise command-first rewrite across all twelve Markdown files. README files remain under 200 lines; preserve unique shared contracts, safety/recovery and owner-controlled publication rules, fix contradictory read-side effects/source-only HTTP/release-default descriptions, and update live references together. Do not relocate unnecessary narrative into new files.
Independent review, focused QA and required local checks pass on the combined candidate; record concrete evidence and any still-unobserved real-Mac/Codex boundaries before candidate closure.

Include advancing stable version/lockfile and exact release notes under the project release value gate. Native hosted CI/archive gates require explicit remote-action agreement. Publication and downloaded-asset checks are read-only post-merge acceptance, never pre-merge claims.

The actual Linux x64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64 archives each contain short installation/use/MCP/update/uninstall instructions and installer help only for that archive's target platform. Windows distinguishes PowerShell/cmd.exe and its direct Node MCP launcher; POSIX recipes use the correct installed paths. Tests check executable commands, platform/runtime requirements and meaningful boundaries rather than explanatory paragraphs.

Remove the obsolete requirement to keep extracted downloads from the release-note policy, validator and future candidate notes together; preserve exact six-section notes, platform commands and all publication/recovery safeguards. Preserve the already handed-off Mac test artifact and create revised builds in a separate output directory.

Each actual archive has exactly one root installation entry: install.sh for Linux x64, Install.command for macOS arm64, Install.cmd for Windows x64. Installer implementation/helpers live under app/scripts; no other root install* or foreign-platform launchers remain. The target entry supports install/update/uninstall/help and preserves exit/error handling, dependency checks, ownership/collision protection and staged replacement.

Upgrading a previous managed archive layout removes obsolete managed root installer files while preserving unrelated/user files and project data. Tests cover real current archives, meaningful old-layout migration, failure paths and target-specific commands; source/local/native acceptance consumers and exact notes/recovery validation agree with the new layout. Preserve already handed-off archives and refresh independent review/QA.

On a genuinely uninitialised default project, shared reads return empty lists/search/batches or zero count; missing single IDs remain not found. Repeat/cache-bypassed reads do not materialise task/schema records or fake tasks. The first real create still works. Core/standalone, CLI, MCP and read-only HTTP agree at their public boundaries.

Keep errors for partial/previously populated/configured missing stores, malformed input/storage, permissions and pending recovery; do not silently repair or erase files. Preserve pagination max 50; count does not require pagination/projection parameters. Demonstrate meaningful regression failures before and passes after; refresh independent review/QA, then provide one current Mac test artifact in dist with a unique name and exact identity.

MCP tool metadata explicitly describes ordinary no_cache=false/omission with freshness-checked cache/JSON fallback, and limit 1–50/default 10 with pagination. All affected read tools agree; advertised machine schema and actual runtime defaults/bounds remain unchanged. Independent review and focused discovered-schema/runtime checks pass.

Prepare exact Outask AI v1.1 release notes, complete candidate closure and PR description after current origin/main integration and necessary local gates. Obtain one exact final push/draft PR/CI/ready agreement; leave owner-only merge/publication sequence intact. Complete explicitly requested v1.0 GitHub Release removal after preserving its exact metadata/notes/three assets locally and confirming v1.0 tag unchanged.

values.goal: Support reliable per-user installation and local CLI/MCP use on the declared platforms.
values.value: Users can install the release despite an unrelated inaccessible PATH entry and follow clear macOS/Codex setup instructions instead of an accidental project-local workaround. Readers can install, run and connect each supported target using concise commands, with shared contracts and delivery rules stated once.
values.observable_result: The reproduced installer failure is eliminated and a clean-shell installed-command/MCP scenario works at the user boundary. Project and generated documentation is short, consistent and specific to each build target.
values.verification: Run the regression against original/fixed installer, native distribution acceptance with a fresh shell PATH, and inspect the actual packaged instructions. Audit all documentation routes and compare the actual three archives/help with their platform's runnable recipes.

title: Keep task JSON readable by default during mutations
scope: Make readable repository-local task JSON the default output of Outask mutations across core/standalone, CLI and MCP. Format new records and changed nonempty arrays/objects with two-space indentation and multiline layout, including string and ID arrays; keep empty collections inline. Preserve bytes of untouched fields/records and avoid whole-store normalization. Align creation, update and lifecycle transfers; retain correct record indentation and a separate closing store bracket/final newline. Do not change console/MCP response formatting, task semantics or add a formatting toggle/global migration.
values: Goal: Outask keeps human-readable repository-local JSON usable without the tracker. Value: contributors can read and review task requirements directly and see bounded meaningful Git diffs after mutations. Immediate verification: inspect actual created/updated/transferred fixture stores and assert readable changed values, byte-identical untouched content and no writes on semantic no-ops.
acceptance: New task records and changed nonempty arrays/objects use readable multiline JSON with two-space indentation at the correct nesting level; string arrays and blocker-ID arrays are not compressed. Empty arrays/objects remain []/{}.

Creating, updating and transferring a task between stores follow the same readable-output contract; task/store closing delimiters have the correct indentation, store closing bracket is on its own line and the file ends with a newline.

Updating one field preserves untouched fields and neighboring records byte-for-byte, including existing formatting and lexemes. Do not reformat entire stores or rewrite legacy compact records outside the mutation scope.

A semantic no-op does not rewrite task stores or advance updated_at; unchanged replacement values retain their original bytes. Preserve existing no-op behavior, validation, IDs, extension fields and concurrency guarantees.

Add regression checks for changed multiline arrays, new arrays and nested objects, creation, transfer, neighboring-record preservation, unchanged fields and semantic no-op byte/timestamp stability. title: Make macOS installation independent of fixed Homebrew library paths
scope: Fix the macOS release installation failure reported as `OutaskAI ./Install.command` followed by `Library not loaded: /opt/homebrew/opt/simdjson/lib/libsimdjson.33.dylib`. The report is one-off; no further information or testing can be requested from that user. Inspect the repository and release installation chain to identify and remove reliance on a developer machine's absolute Homebrew paths or a specific external dylib filename. Keep unnecessary third-party packages out of the repository/distribution. Detect required external programs through normal executable discovery, document and check their minimum supported versions, accept compatible newer versions, and offer installation guidance or an explicit installation action when a prerequisite is missing or too old. Homebrew must not be required merely because it was present on the build machine. Do not treat arbitrary native-library ABI versions as interchangeable or use dylib-name symlinks as a fix. Keep the scope to the macOS installer, its actual prerequisites and affected distribution checks/documentation.
acceptance: The shipped macOS installation/startup chain does not require /opt/homebrew/opt/simdjson/lib/libsimdjson.33.dylib or another developer-specific absolute third-party library path; record the identified source of the dependency, without claiming the unavailable user's environment was confirmed.

Required external programs are discovered independently of a single package-manager prefix. Their minimum supported versions are documented and checked; supported versions at or above the minimum proceed without requiring one exact package release.

Missing or too-old prerequisites produce a clear actionable message and an offer/instructions to install or upgrade before a dependent executable can fail with a raw loader error. Check the case where Homebrew itself is absent; do not silently require it or install software.

Verify the actual macOS archive on native Apple Silicon in an environment without the reported simdjson file: with supported prerequisites, run Install.command and an installed CLI/MCP smoke check successfully. Record evidence in this task; original reporter participation is not required.

Focused checks cover a missing prerequisite, a version below the minimum, the minimum supported version and a supported newer version, including discovery outside /opt/homebrew. Keep Linux and Windows installation contracts unchanged.
Update existing installation/prerequisite documentation to match the final behavior; do not add unnecessary bundled packages or promise compatibility with arbitrary native-library ABIs.

title: Add latest-release updates to platform installers
scope: Make every published stable release explicitly become GitHub's Latest release, while prereleases do not replace it. Add an update action alongside install and uninstall to the packaged Linux, macOS and Windows installers. The action must resolve the latest stable GitHub release, download the matching supported-platform archive and reuse the existing installation path so user task data and configuration are preserved. Keep prompts, output, documentation and failure handling concise; do not add a separate updater service or background update mechanism.
acceptance: Publishing a stable release explicitly marks it Latest, and GitHub's latest-release API resolves that release; a prerelease does not replace the latest stable release.

The packaged commands ./install.sh update, ./Install.command update and Install.cmd update upgrade an older installed release to the latest stable release on Linux x64, macOS Apple silicon and Windows x64 respectively.
After update, tasks --version reports the latest release and fresh CLI/MCP launches use it, while project tasks, user configuration and the existing compatible-session behavior are preserved.
An already-current installation reports a concise no-change result; resolution, download or installation failure leaves the working installed release usable and emits an actionable error.

Focused installer and release-publication checks cover latest selection, platform asset selection, successful update, no-change and failure behavior; required project CI passes and concise operator documentation lists the update commands.

Preserve records, IDs, unknown fields, unrelated files and explicit external path choices; stop for resolution rather than deleting installations whose ownership is not established. Use one stable platform Outask application/config/cache root and retain only necessary external integrations. Windows writer coordination moves to the fixed OS-user Outask root/locks; require completed writes and closed prior sessions before starting the new generation, without live-session or mixed-generation compatibility claims. POSIX coordination retains its current fixed namespace. Complete application/config/cache uninstall remains task 12. Keep test user/config/cache/temp state isolated and close fixture clients before removing only fixture-owned coordination files. acceptance: Installed commands outask and tasks share arguments, operations, help, output, errors, exit codes and one installation. Outask is the displayed product name and outask the canonical service identifier.

Current runtime, manifests, source paths, tests, generated archives, documentation, agent guidance and release tooling contain no retired product-name spelling or its command alias, including compatibility recognition.

Produce exactly three Outask-<version>-<target>.tar.gz assets with Outask/ extraction roots for Linux x64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64. Publication, download verification and recovery enforce only this current naming contract.

Remove superseded compatibility archive generation and immutable consumer fixtures for the retired identity. Previously published releases and Git history are not rewritten; current tooling need not support their retired naming.

CLI help/version, fresh MCP metadata and source HTTP identity use Outask/outask. Inspect actual Linux running process titles and document OS/client-controlled display limitations without claiming universal control.
Existing task records, IDs, unknown JSON fields, task-domain operation names, task stores, schemas and project metadata/recovery filenames remain usable without a data-format migration.

Fresh installation uses ~/.local/share/outask on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/Outask on macOS and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Outask on Windows. Application files, default config.json and disposable cache/ use that root without a releases layer or version accumulation; explicit external paths remain supported.

Recognise only current application branding and supported task-domain installation layouts. Preserve unrelated files and configuration; refuse unknown command/destination ownership with actionable replacement instructions. Do not retain or manufacture retired branded paths.

Windows writers use <OS-user-home>/AppData/Local/Programs/Outask/locks independent of HOME/cache/config/temp overrides. Document the coordination-generation boundary: finish writes and close all prior sessions before new writers start. Do not migrate or delete live locks or claim mixed-generation compatibility. POSIX retains its fixed existing coordination namespace.

Inventory necessary POSIX command links, shell PATH/profile blocks including ZDOTDIR, Windows launcher/PATH integration, explicit registry paths and installed Git hooks/client references. Repeated current installation/update consolidates only confirmed current managed entries and preserves unrelated content.

Verify both installed commands, CLI reads/help/errors, fresh MCP connections and source HTTP identity, plus install/reinstall/update/rollback/uninstall acceptance from the actual native archive. Hosted native CI supplies unavailable OS/Node evidence.

Run lifecycle, cache and migration checks in isolated HOME/config/cache/temp fixtures. Close MCP/HTTP clients and writer children before removing fixture-owned coordination files; do not alter operator profiles/configuration or remove unrelated coordination files.

Update README with the lightweight personal-project/AI-harness positioning and readable active/completed/archived task history alongside code. Use Outask as the product name; describe AI as the use case, not a suffix in the name.

Update owning contracts and setup/release instructions consistently, record actual gate evidence and limitations in this task, and complete independent review/QA and candidate closure before any final push agreement.
